Meanwhile, a young man named Jules (Marcus Thomas) wants to re-create his happiest Christmas memory.

Known as the resident tough cop due to his aggressive tactics, he gets knocked sideways when his girlfriend becomes one of the murder victims. With his partner, Storm Anderson, in tow, Jacob casts the rules aside and infiltrates the seedy criminal underworld of the city looking to avenge his lover's death and put an end to the killings.

programme.title: End Game
programme.desc: When Secret Service agent Alex Thomas (Cuba Gooding Jr.) acts too slowly to stop a crazed shooter, the president of the United States (Jack Scalia) is brutally shot in the middle of a press conference. In the wake of his death, journalist Kate Crawford (Angie Harmon) begins to suspect a massive conspiracy is afoot. Crawford convinces a skeptical Thomas to help her, and the two struggle to unravel the mystery behind the assassination -- before they become the next targets.

programme.title: Reach Me

programme.title: Survivor
programme.desc: Framed for crimes she did not commit, a British diplomat tries to prevent a terrorist attack on New York City.

programme.title: Edison
programme.desc: Ambitious young reporter Pollack (Justin Timberlake) suspects insidious corruption in his town's elite police unit, known as F.R.A.T., and finds a friendly source in Deed (LL Cool J), a dissatisfied member of the squad. With Deed's information and the backing of his publisher, Ashford (Morgan Freeman), and a crusading lawyer, Wallace (Kevin Spacey), Pollack infiltrates the secretive police cabal. He finds himself in over his head, however, when he discovers the true extent of the criminality.

programme.title: Smothered
programme.desc: A food critic (Carly Pope) finds her life turned upside down when her uninhibited mother (Christine Baranski) arrives unannounced at Christmas. Desperate to offload her, she enlists the help of a chef (Bobby Cannavale) - with surprising results.

programme.title: Aquarium: An Aquatic Life
programme.desc: Join us as we delve into the inner workings of the Two Oceans Aquarium and meet the team who keep the machine running! Learn how they cater for hundreds of different dietary requirements, how they keep up with the demand of life-giving water and meet the new arrivals to the aquarium; from the six-legged spider crabs of Japan, to the tiny turtles in need of rehabilitation. We'll move behind the glass to reveal the secrets of Africa's premier Aquarium!

programme.title: Wildest Survival
programme.desc: Many animals have evolved chemicals to enhance their chance of survival: some scorpions literally drug their potential mates, others use their poisons to defend or kill. The world of venoms and poisons, the apparatus designed to deliver the payload and the strategies that animals employ to use them most effectively is a rich and varied example of natural selection and evolution in action.

programme.title: History of Life on Earth - Life in the Sea
programme.desc: Our planet is one of oceans, and it was this great mass of water that gave birth to Earth's greatest creation - life

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: Lions, Chimpanzees, Turtles, Roe Deer, Gannets Reproduction is not only a concern of the young and restless: this episode of Aging in the Wild brings a light-hearted look at the issue of sexuality and camaraderie in older animals. We illustrate, for example, the link between the age of an elephant and its reproductive success. What are the reproductive benefits of these animals as they grow older?

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: Bighorn Sheep, Elk, Male Elephants, Marmots, Baboons, Rhinos Observing two massive elk clashing their antlers is to witness a true demonstration of power. For other species, such as the European marmot, remaining in power is a matter of collaborating with family and community. Are these animals forced to give up their hard-won social status as they age? Through this lens, we take a deep and entertaining look at the challenges faced by those in power ... and what it takes to stay there.

programme.title: Nature's Most Dangerous
programme.desc: Few things make us shiver like the thought of falling prey to one of the world's great predators. With teeth, claws, stings and venom, they inflict death on their prey, and instil fear in us. But who's not a thrill seeker among us? We humans love to put ourselves at risk and lap up the thrill of living dan-gerously. And to fuel our fetish for fear, we turn to the animal kingdom, imagining close shaves with all the planet's most dangerous creatures.

programme.title: World of the Wild
programme.desc: The Arctic is alive with a fascinating assortment of wildlife and species that are unique to this Polar environment. Most of are rarely or never seen outside the Arctic Circle. They live and thrive in a hostile environment of ice, polar desert, wind-swept open tundra, ancient glacial formations, sub zero sea temperatures and an incredible variety of geographical topo-graphy from open plain and valleys to mountainous peaks and deep water fiords.

programme.title: Wildest Places: Pacific
programme.desc: Wildest Places explores some of the most incredible natural habitats on earth & a diverse range of wildlife.

programme.title: April (Nature's Calendar)
programme.desc: aster, a time of babies, easter eggs are everywhere as birds get busy breeding, lambs dance around fields and cute baby bunnies emerge from their borrows. Migrants like ospreys and puffins return to their breeding sites. Migrants can come in all shapes and sizes and for different reasons. Hammerhead sharks swarm around Galapagos and take advantage of cleaning services on the reef.

programme.title: Hannah Goes to Namibia
programme.desc: The poaching of rhinos for their horn has brought these animals to the brink of extinction. Namibia's black rhinos are hard to find. The Save The Rhino Trust has been fighting for the protection of the pachyderms every day for 30 years under the most adverse conditions. Hannah Emde accompanies the anti-poaching unit through the semi-desert for a day. She learns how difficult it is to track the animals and can hardly believe her luck when she finds a mother with her calf.

programme.title: Hunters of the Forest
programme.desc: Forests are dark, shady habitats, realms of shadows perfect for predators to lurk. The dense plant growth facilitates a wealth of prey species, and cunning predators of all shapes and sizes have adapted to exploit every niche. Whether crawling on the forest floor, gliding through the trees or stalking the shadows in between, hunters have mastered the terrain in every type of forest imagina-ble.

programme.title: Hidden Japan
programme.desc: The culture of Japan is incredible. But there are also more than 130 mammals and 600 bird species dwelling in Japan's 6,852 islands.

programme.title: World's Wildest City: Anchorage
programme.desc: There are more Caribou in Alaska than people! Across the Arctic, they're the lifeblood of many remote communities. But human expansion, and wild predators, have led to their rapid decline. Out on the tundra, Caribou are the prey of choice for Alaska's carnivores, and at a ranch on the edge of Anchorage, the reindeer are at constant risk from the area's wolves and brown bears. The people of Anchorage have vowed to protect them, but will their help be enough for the Caribou to survive?

programme.title: Hidden Japan
programme.desc: The culture of Japan is incredible. But there are also more than 130 mammals and 600 bird species dwelling in Japan's 6,852 islands.

programme.title: Mother's Day
programme.desc: Being a wild mum is one of the toughest jobs on earth. From the second a mother gives birth, everything changes. No longer footloose and fancy free, they find themselves completely responsible for tiny, delicate little lives - lives that would be helpless without them. For some, being a mother comes naturally, whilst for others it will take a little practoce. But while the responsibility is immense, being a mum is also incredible.

programme.title: Aquarium: An Aquatic Life
programme.desc: This episode will introduce you to some of the Aquariums most weird and wonderful inhabitants. From upside-down Jellyfish to male Seahorses giving birth, these wacky residents make up the enchanting world that keeps guests coming to through the Aquarium doors! But other pressing issues keep the staff busy, from keeping the peace between man and seal, to preparing a new gigantic predator tank, there's not a minute to rest in the life of an Aquarist!

programme.title: Destination Wild - Wild Colombia
programme.desc: Chiribiquete is an unknown world, hidden deep within Colombia's Amazon. Pre-historic towers, waterfalls and deep canyons lie surrounded by rivers, lakes and rainforests bursting with life. Scientists have only guessed at what else lies beneath this impenetrable pristine jungle - until now. Biologist Blanca Huertas from England's Natural History Museum, and Colombian-born nature photographer Francisco Forero, head deep into the heart of nowhere.

programme.title: Wild Wolverine
programme.desc: To many the wolverine is the stuff of movie superheroes. To others they are a creature of myth and legend. They look like a weird hybrid between wolf, bear and skunk and are some of the toughest, strongest and most aggressive animals around. In the sub-arctic forests of Siberia survival is an expert skill. The creatures of the far north strike a delicate balance and must show ingenuity and cunning if they are to survive.

programme.title: Hawaii: Paradise in the Pacific
programme.desc: In epsiode one we take a look at Kaua'i - the oldest island in the archipelago. Kaua'i's isolation for thousands of years led to an increased rate of evolution. In a relatively short time, new species are formed here, many animals and plants can only be found here. But they are in danger. On the shield volcano Waiʻaleʻale - the rainiest place on earth, scientists like Lukas Behnke are fighting for the preservation of endangered native animals and plants.

programme.title: Our Big Blue Backyard
programme.desc: It's a miracle the first seafarers ever found the Cook Islands/ Kūki 'Airani scattered across two million square kilometres of the Pacific Ocean. But every year, these tropical islands become the destination for over three thousand Humpback whales who've undertaken one of the longest migrations on the planet. They come here to socialise, mate, and raise their young.

programme.title: Our Big Blue Backyard
programme.desc: Te Moananui a Toi/ The Hauraki Gulf lies on the doorstep of New Zealand's largest city. Every summer millions of visitors from the tropics converge here, all lured by a unique seasonal smorgasbord. Giant oceanic manta rays, rarely filmed in these waters, glide into the gulf. Bryde's whales are also primed for the feasting season, alongside common dolphins, and bronze whaler sharks. In the sky above rare black petrels stalk the dolphins to survive.
programme.sub-title: Te Moananui a Toi/ The Hauraki Gulf

programme.title: Wildest Survival
programme.desc: For every baby animal born, billions don't make it. Drought, flood, famine and predation; babies are born into a harsh world. The odds are so heavily stacked against some animals that it's a miracle any of their youngsters survive at-all. In this episode we discover the incredible lengths that nature's parents go to in order to ensure their progeny's survival.

programme.title: Secret Life of Baby Owls
programme.desc: Owls - with their huge eyes, flat faces and distinctive hoot - they are truly iconic!creatures. But how much do we really know about these mysterious nocturnal birds? We're about to find out as we follow the fate of new born baby owls as they grow up and learn to fly.

programme.title: World's Wildest City: Anchorage
programme.desc: Alaska one of the last true wildernesses on earth. With 600 square miles of pristine habitat this state is home to an abundance of wildlife. Herds of caribou roam the plains, wolves stalk in the forest and the brown bears are the kings of the rivers. But you don't always have to head to the wild to come face to face with an animal. In the city of Anchorage the wildlife is a lot closer than you think, because a city with so much green space means everywhere is fair game for its wild neighbours.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: Salmon, Bears, Beluga Whales, Naked Mole Rat, Bacteria, Aspen Trees In this episode, we explore how different animal species react to impending death. We explore the factors that lead animals to their final resting places: disease, injury, predation, drought, famine. Some species, such as the naked mole rat, while not immortal, seem to be able to effectively protect themselves from certain diseases such as cancer.

programme.title: Hannah Goes to Namibia
programme.desc: Hannah Emde tries to illuminate the subject of trophy hunting from all sides. She talks to the Khwe chief, villagers and game guards in the Zambezi region. She meets a trophy hunter and follows the topic back to Germany, where she exchanges ideas with Izak Smit, the Chairperson of Desert Lions Human Relations Aid, Delhra in short.
programme.sub-title: Trophy hunting - just killing or conservation?

programme.title: May (Nature's Calendar)
programme.desc: While we celebrate may day, the coming of summer, there are many changes going on in the world. As snows finally melt in the mountains of Europe, chamois lambs have the chance to test out their climbing skills and explore their vertical home, watching all the time for eagles, their main predators. On the vast plains of the Russian the weird looking saiga antelope have their calves, while Florida enters its fire season and even the everglades can burn

programme.title: Wildest Islands
programme.desc: Between the continents of North and South America is a tropical paradise: the Caribbean. This archipelago of over 7,000 islands and reefs lies within the crystal clear waters of the Caribbean Sea. From just a few metres wide, to hundreds of kilometres across, every island is different, and each has its own unique wildlife.
programme.sub-title: The Caribbean: The Wild Side of Paradise

programme.title: Animal Record Breakers
programme.desc: We love to measure aspects of life at its extremes. The biggest, the tallest, heaviest, fastest, slowest - even the rarest. The creatures that hold the records for these categories are some of the most interesting in the natural world. Some are familiar and iconic, but it's also important to recognise some of the more surprising record breakers. These quirky and unusual animals that often go ignored are inventive, ingenious and awe-inspiring.

programme.title: Destination Wild: Wild Madagascar
programme.desc: Millions of years ago, hundreds of castaway creatures crash-landed on Madagascar's rugged shores. Isolated from the mainland, evolution went into overdrive. Of almost a quarter of a million species found on the island are unique. This myriad of bizarre life forms had a huge impact on the early human settlers - one particular group of primates shaped their culture, fuelling folklore and legend that still guides their lives today. Limited Rights Available: Worldwide, Free TV Only

programme.title: Hidden UK
programme.desc: For its tiny size the UK is a hugely varied landscape with a surprising collection of remarkable and awe-inspiring wildlife.

programme.title: Nature's Cutest
programme.desc: As we all know the natural world can be tough and challenging at times, but it can also be nothing short of adorable. Fluffy white seals, wobbly-kneed fawns, playing polar bear cubs, adorable teddy bear-like koalas - so much cute it would be impossible to decide which was the most adorable. But why do we consider some animals cute and others not? What it is about them that makes us fall in love? Perhaps it's those animals that remind us of ourselves?

programme.title: Destination Wild - Wild Islands
programme.desc: The Caribbean has been shaped by millions of years of unstoppable volcanic forces and ferocious hurricanes, creating a network of 7,000 islands, each one more unique than the next. From islets only a few miles long to landmasses with towering peaks, the habitats of this tropical paradise range from lush rainforests hiding untold species to multi-coloured coral reefs teeming with marine life.

programme.title: Wildest Places: Pacific
programme.desc: Wildest Places explores some of the most incredible natural habitats on earth & a diverse range of wildlife.

programme.title: World of the Wild
programme.desc: It might look uniform from the air, as we fly over it, but the oceans are deep and varied. The underwater landscape is made up of continental shelves, volcanoes, mountains, valleys, trenches and large, flat plains similar to the landscape on land only on a much larger scale. Ocean habitats come in all forms. Under water creatures make homes wherever survival is assured.

programme.title: Our Big Blue Backyard
programme.desc: The top of New Zealand's South Island is a landscape of two halves. To the West, one of the longest natural sandbars on the planet curves protectively around Golden Bay. To the East, mountains sink into the sea, their drowned river valleys forming the Marlborough Sounds. Turbulent currents connect them, both treacherous and full of riches.
programme.sub-title: Top of the South/ Te Tau Ihu

programme.title: Sexy Beasts
programme.desc: Driven by surging hormones, every creature on the planet, big or small, will do whatever it takes to find and secure a mate. For some this will take the fight of their lives, while others must preen, prance and party their way to success. From one night stands and group sex to lifelong love and unbreakable bonds, when it comes to finding a mate the animal kingdom has it all. The need to breed manifests itself in all sorts of wonderful antics, displays and behaviours.

programme.title: History of Life on Earth - Rise of the Giants
programme.desc: In the great story of life, reptiles were one of the first major players. For 180 million years they ruled the land, seas and skies - this was the rise of the giants.

programme.title: Lions Rule
programme.desc: The Lion, Africa's ultimate predator. An essay in power and agility, famed for the cut-throat gang and the killer instinct. Lions are known as the kings of the jungle yet their homeland is an open grassland rather than rainforest. In the African plains prey-rich real estate can be hard to come by, and lions work together to ensure no one claims their territory and usurps their crown.

programme.title: The Enchanted Forest
programme.desc: To spend a day in the forest, from dawn to dusk, is to bathe in nature. There's enchantment at every turn. Throughout the day the cast of characters in the forest changes, from foraging bears to playing fox cubs, dashing hummingbirds and dancing butterflies. But it's as twilight descends, that the most enchanting side of the forest is revealed. Time to watch a firework display curtesy of fireflies. They are the real magicians of the enchanted forest.

programme.title: Wild and Alive
programme.desc: On the savannah of southern Africa, rains have turned the land green and lush. It's the time of plenty and for the cast of wild characters here, cashing in is priority number one. From polecat to aardwolf, some of the continent's most seldom seen creatures are out to make the most of the abundance. Some families gorge on the plentiful grasses, while for others there's no such thing as an easy meal, even at this time of year.

programme.title: Wild Uruguay
programme.desc: Uruguay's biodiversity is surprisingly greater than one would expect. We will find out why as we embark on a journey through its ecosystems and landscapes to discover its fauna. Today we know that Uruguay is more than just the outermost edge of the Pampas, as the country holds a range of ecosystems. Within its borders, species of the Pampas come face to face with species of the Atlantic Forest, the Misiones rainforest, and the Chaco forest, giving rise to unexpected encounters.

programme.title: History of Life on Earth - Journey to the Land
programme.desc: As the first landmasses emerged from prehistoric seas, animals took their first steps on dry land. The explosion of life that followed changed the world forever.

programme.title: Hidden Russia
programme.desc: There's no doubt Russia has it all: from the subtropics to the arctic and the Atlantic to the Pacific; giant lakes, active volcanoes and endless forests.

programme.title: Destination Wild - Wild Europe
programme.desc: The story of Europe's living waters begins at great altitude. Melt waters from the highest snow-capped peaks feed some of the greatest rivers. On their relentless downward journey, streams and rivers have carved through all of Europe's greatest landscapes. Gorges, lakes and wetlands are home to an incredible array of wildlife and seas and oceans have sculpted a coastline of endless variety.

programme.title: Hidden Australia
programme.desc: Sometimes called the biggest island on Earth, Australia is a subcontinent of incredible diversity, beauty, danger and downright weirdness.

programme.title: Wildest Survival
programme.desc: In this episode we explore why and how animals fight and reveal the ways in which they are programmed to survive at all costs. Most animals will defend themselves against predators, but many also do battle with members of the same species. Animals fight for two main reasons: for a mate or to defend their young or territory. And when animals fight, it can often be to the death.

programme.title: Fight for Territory
programme.desc: Biological instinct is driven by three things: the desire to stay alive, to find food and to breed. But to do all these things, animals first need a home. Out in the wilderness a safe place to call home can be the difference between life and death. A place to secure meals, raise their families and hide from danger. Ideal spots are in short supply and well worth fighting for!

programme.title: March (Nature's Calendar)
programme.desc: As northern forests become carpeted by bluebells and wood anemones, and damp corners become singles bars for frogs and a toads, hailing the first hint of spring sun, South Africa needs a break from the heat, fire season is in full swing, threatening the fynbos and the extraordinary animals living in them. Ground squirrels get inventive to find shade. Gray whales migrate up the Californian coast, passing colonies of sea otters. March is a month of change

programme.title: Wildest Survival
programme.desc: Whether by wing, fin or hoof, epic migrations are among nature's most awe-inspiring events. Animals undertake these arduous journeys, for many reasons: to find a mate, to give birth, or to move to new feeding grounds. And danger lurks at every turn. In this episode we discover the lengths they go to in order to survive.

programme.title: Wildest Islands
programme.desc: Lying like a teardrop in the Indian Ocean, Sri Lanka is an island that defies convention. Poised just six degrees above the equator, it's less than 75,000 km sq in size. But it has enough wildlife to rival a continent, and it's all down to its complicated climate and geography.

programme.title: Wolves - Power of the Pack
programme.desc: From arctic tundra to the great planes, the kingdom of the wolf extends across the entire northern hemisphere. They are icons of the wilderness, spectacular creatures that live and die by the sword. Though magnificent predators on their own, the feature that perhaps makes wolves so iconic is the pack. The close bonds, complex communication and sheer muscle of a team of wolves is almost unstoppable. And the pack's not just the day job, it's the cornerstone of family life for a wolf.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: The Great Deceiver. Seducer of the masses. The Bringer of Armageddon. Every culture and religion on the planet believes that an evil one will usher in the end of days. But who is this Anti-Christ? And how can we hope to stop him?

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: We rely on machines for virtually every aspect of modern life. Have we reached the point where we need them more than they need us? If technology goes too far, too fast, there may be a time where we are no longer at the top of the evolutionary food chain.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: From military radar to Navy aircraft, sightings of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena have become more frequent of late and been measured on ever more sophisticated technology. It has lead to unprecedented acceptance of alien contact across the globe, including by the US government. What could these visitors be after? Is it the potential energy stored in the Earth's oceans?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Several US presidents throughout history have described encounters with UAPs. Is there already an agreement in place between our world leaders and intelligent alien life? And if so, who is keeping that information from the public and why?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: In 1998 Astronauts captured images of a satellite in Earth's orbit. Is it the same alien object that Nicola Tesla detected in 1899, an alien probe known as the Black Knight? And in 2017 scientists discovered another mysterious satellite from outside our solar system. What could explain Oumuamua's artificial trajectory?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: According to physics, time travel is possible. So could it be that UAPs aren't coming from somewhere else, but from some when else. Could these UAPs be us, from the future?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Certain structures on our planet have stood the test of time and continue to astonish mankind. So much so, that alien intervention in their construction thousands of years ago, has yet to be ruled out.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: In July of 2023, David Grusch, a former high ranking US Intelligence officer testified to a US government Oversight Committee that there are alien spacecraft located at secret facilities in the US.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Some places in the world, record more UAP sightings than the rest. So many so, in fact, that people flock from all over the world just for the chance to glimpse a flying saucer.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: As the Fermi Paradox states, the possibilities that there is advanced life in the universe is surprisingly high. And if the universe is so old, why haven't we had any contact with extraterrestrial life?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: There is physical evidence of alien activity that has been hidden from the public for years. It is starting to be revealed.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: It is likely that aliens exist in a universe as large as ours. How would they navigate those vast distances and potentially visit us on earth?

programme.title: EXtraterrestrials: They are Among Us
programme.desc: Explore mysterious sightings spanning millennia, from ancient rock art to recent encounters. Witness strange lights over Barranco de Badajoz and a peculiar being at 'El Condesito' farm in Huelva. Encounter enigmatic humanoids on Conil beaches. Hear from witnesses to unravel the uncanny connection between past depictions and present sightings.

programme.title: EXtraterrestrials: They are Among Us
programme.desc: Places for contact (by appointment): There are places on the planet where contact with these supposed entities that come from other worlds turns out to be more intense than in other places; And it has been like that for thousands of years.

programme.title: Secrets of UFOs
programme.desc: Crop circles have been reported around the globe for more than a century. They appear usually in complete darkness and often instantaneously. Some are clearly hoaxes. Others are inexplicable, with no evidence of human activity. This program asks questions like why do crops undergo changes at the cellular level and what are the strange lights seen over the fields where crop circles are found?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Our world is changing. Temperatures are climbing. Ocean levels are rising. Giant storms are becoming more frequent and intense. Super-viruses are thriving in this new environment. At the same time, alien activity is also on the rise.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Humanity has been plagued by international conflicts and epic powers since the dawn of time. Perhaps our greatest failure is constant strife and division. Could an alien threat force humans to form a united front?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: For decades, eyewitnesses have reported UFOs crashing to Earth all over the nation. Most are never found. Some believe crashed UFOs may contain alien technology that could change the course of history

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: For decades, citizen UFOlogists have coordinated alien information-sharing networks, subverting the classified intelligence of their governments. What do these classified documents say about the way that our governments watch the skies?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: The sun. It's an immense powerhouse on a scale that almost defies the imagination. And it's the source of all life here on Earth. But what if that power was being tampered with? Are UFOs really visiting our Sun?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Each year, there are thousands of UFO sightings all over the world. What are these different kind of UFOs? What is each craft's purpose? What powers them and how they are controlled? And most importantly- who is flying them?

programme.title: The Other Side: Secrets of the Paranormal World
programme.desc: Pre-titles and the explanation of premise for believer and non-believer. Origins of the Devil which has the explainer and discussion with Matteo Borrini/Deborah Hyde. Derren Brown Interview. Ouija Section, explanation. Christopher French interview. Haunting section/explanation, interview with Derren Brown, Uri Geller and Jayne Harris. Controlled experiments.

programme.title: Ghost Dimension
programme.desc: Located in Gran Canaria, there is one house that locals refuse to enter and that is, The House of Fear. Ghostly shadows, loud banging and demonic voices have all been reported here and the Ghost Dimension team will investigate these claims tonight.

programme.title: Ghost Dimension Flying Solo
programme.desc: Sean continues the investigation at Morley Market and appears to be followed by a spirit person that wants to touch him and distract him from investigating certain parts of the main hall. Will he uncover who this spirit is?
programme.sub-title: Shadow Menace Haunting Morley Market - Part 2

programme.title: Paranormal Files: Extraordinary Stories - Ordinary People
programme.desc: In 1995, a small UK village was disrupted by a brutal fire that destroyed its town hall. To this day, no culprit has emerged - were otherworldly forces responsible?

programme.title: Paranormal Files: Extraordinary Stories - Ordinary People
programme.desc: Bonnybridge, a village in Scotland, has long been shrouded in paranormal mystery. Are the flying objects hovering above its skies connected to alien life? Explore the mystery in this episode.

programme.title: Paranormal Files: Extraordinary Stories - Ordinary People
programme.desc: Since its origin in 1196, Micklegate Bar, a massive entrance to the city of York, has been host to royal powers, Lords, and also some other guests, those from a world beyond ours.

programme.title: War On Witches
programme.desc: In the late 16th century Europe was in the grip of a witch hunt fever. Thousands were tortured and burnt at the stake. The church was fully behind this terrifying crusade. In France and Germany alone up to 40,000 people may have been killed as witches. England and Scotland were almost untouched by witch persecutions until King James himself decided to launch his own, personal war on witchcraft.

programme.title: Nazi Creatures
programme.desc: Hitler, Goring, Himmler: the three architects of the Final Solution. They, like many other high ranking Nazis, shared a fascination with the animal world. In the last days of the Nazi regime, Hitler risked his life every day, leaving the safety of the bunker to walk his beloved dog, Blondi. But the Nazis' interest went beyond love of their pets or the animal welfare laws they introduced.

programme.title: Mysteries of Stonehenge
programme.desc: On the grassy chalk-land of the Salisbury plain, two hours southwest of London, there looms a remarkable stone monument. It certainly seems that Stonehenge is a silent remnant of another age...a reminder of man's primordial beginnings. There are countless legends about its origin and purpose. Who built it? How and when was it built? And most intriguing of all, what is it?

programme.title: The Magic of Houdini: The Illusions and Stunts of Harry Houdini
programme.desc: Having been fascinated with magic since he was a boy, Alan Davies explores the life of illusionist and stunt performer, Harry Houdini, who became one of the most successful entertainers in the world. Alan holds his breath underwater, lies on a bed of nails, gets strung upside down in a straitjacket and takes an exclusive look at David Copperfield's collection of Houdini artefacts in Vegas.

programme.title: The Conspiracy Show with Richard Syrett
programme.desc: Richard travels to Kent in the south of England to investigate reports of werewolf sightings. He meets with an acclaimed paranormal investigator in New York's Central Park who separates fact from fiction regarding the legend of the werewolf, and a journalist describes eye-witness accounts of a bi-pedal, wolf-like creature said to be haunting a lonely stretch of road in Wisconsin.

programme.title: The Conspiracy Show with Richard Syrett
programme.desc: Richard travels to London to investigate various theories revolving around the tragic death of Diana, The former Princess of Wales. Was the fatal car crash in a Paris tunnel in August 1997 a result of a drunken driver or was she murdered? Was she pregnant with the child of Dodi Al Fayed? Was she perceived as a threat to the Royal Family?
programme.sub-title: The Death of Princess Diana: Tragic Car Accident or Murder Most Foul?

programme.title: EXtraterrestrials: They are Among Us
programme.desc: What can lead a military man to draw his service weapon in his own base, and completely unload the magazine of his rifle? In the cases that we are going to analyze, these military men claim to have witnessed the appearance of strange humanoid beings.

programme.title: EXtraterrestrials: They are Among Us
programme.desc: Explore mysterious sightings spanning millennia, from ancient rock art to recent encounters. Witness strange lights over Barranco de Badajoz and a peculiar being at 'El Condesito' farm in Huelva. Encounter enigmatic humanoids on Conil beaches. Hear from witnesses to unravel the uncanny connection between past depictions and present sightings.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Our world is changing. Temperatures are climbing. Ocean levels are rising. Giant storms are becoming more frequent and intense. Super-viruses are thriving in this new environment. At the same time, alien activity is also on the rise.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Humanity has been plagued by international conflicts and epic powers since the dawn of time. Perhaps our greatest failure is constant strife and division. Could an alien threat force humans to form a united front?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Pyramids are found all over the world and from different time periods in human history. Did humans build the pyramids by themselves - or did they have help? Some experts believe pyramids across the world are part of a grand alien design.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: For decades, eyewitnesses have reported UFOs crashing to Earth all over the nation. Most are never found. Some believe crashed UFOs may contain alien technology that could change the course of history

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Scientists believe that Stargates are doorways to wormholes in time. As it turns out, the government may have already known that. We'll reveal the secret location of stargates around the world and tell you who is trying to open them and why.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files counts down the top 10 conspiracies of all time: (10) the moon landing hoax, (9) MK Ultra mind control experiments, (8) the secret Area 51 air force base, (7) the H.A.A.R.P. antenna installation, (6) Chemtrails in the atmosphere, (5) the New World Order, (4) the Jesus was married conspiracy, (3) the Roswell incident, (2) Hitler's Death, and (1) the JFK assassination.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files looks at how the Soviet Union and the United States sponsored experiments in remote viewing during the Cold War. It also looks at how the CIA spent $20 million dollars investigating remote viewing as a part of Project Stargate. It also discusses how remote viewers were used to look for the Mars Observer and a possible Mars Base.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: There are three types of close encounters, sightings, fleeting interactions, aliens taking humans for extended periods. We meet real people who have experienced alien life up close.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: From military radar to Navy aircraft, sightings of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena have become more frequent of late and been measured on ever more sophisticated technology. It has lead to unprecedented acceptance of alien contact across the globe, including by the US government. What could these visitors be after? Is it the potential energy stored in the Earth's oceans?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Several US presidents throughout history have described encounters with UAPs. Is there already an agreement in place between our world leaders and intelligent alien life? And if so, who is keeping that information from the public and why?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: In 1998 Astronauts captured images of a satellite in Earth's orbit. Is it the same alien object that Nicola Tesla detected in 1899, an alien probe known as the Black Knight? And in 2017 scientists discovered another mysterious satellite from outside our solar system. What could explain Oumuamua's artificial trajectory?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: According to physics, time travel is possible. So could it be that UAPs aren't coming from somewhere else, but from some when else. Could these UAPs be us, from the future?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Certain structures on our planet have stood the test of time and continue to astonish mankind. So much so, that alien intervention in their construction thousands of years ago, has yet to be ruled out.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: In July of 2023, David Grusch, a former high ranking US Intelligence officer testified to a US government Oversight Committee that there are alien spacecraft located at secret facilities in the US.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: Some places in the world, record more UAP sightings than the rest. So many so, in fact, that people flock from all over the world just for the chance to glimpse a flying saucer.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: As the Fermi Paradox states, the possibilities that there is advanced life in the universe is surprisingly high. And if the universe is so old, why haven't we had any contact with extraterrestrial life?

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: There is physical evidence of alien activity that has been hidden from the public for years. It is starting to be revealed.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: The list of global threats to the human race is long. But could Earth's armed forces be facing a new enemy that is literally out of this world? We expose military evidence that could prove world governments have long been preparing for the next great global conflict-a real-life a war of the worlds.

programme.title: UFO Casebook
programme.desc: Of all the various kinds of UFO related phenomenon that has materialized, the so called light spheres certainly hold a particularly important place. These objects have recently gained great popularity thanks in part to the studies conducted by Dr. Eltjo Haselhoff, who believes that these light spheres could be the cause behind crop circles. The lights began to appear many years ago...but why?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: All around the world, millions of people from all walks of life are reporting the same thing. Aliens have arrived on Earth. Is this the biggest, most well organized hoax in history? Can millions of witnesses worldwide be wrong? In fact many experts believe, all signs point to a massive global cover-up. We unseal the truth behind the most active alien hotspots on Earth.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Everyday, UFOs are spotted in skies all over the world. But of all the planets in the known galaxy, why have they come to Earth? Are aliens here to seize Earth's riches? And how far does their mission go?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: An extraterrestrial threat. A top secret organization. Has the US made contact with aliens? Experts believe they have. And an ultra top secret organization is calling all the shots. Get ready for the untold story of Majestic 12.

programme.title: Alien Disclosure Files
programme.desc: From military radar to Navy aircraft, sightings of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena have become more frequent of late and been measured on ever more sophisticated technology. It has lead to unprecedented acceptance of alien contact across the globe, including by the US government. What could these visitors be after? Is it the potential energy stored in the Earth's oceans?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Aborigines have the oldest continuous culture on Earth. Rock paintings and ancient legends suggest that aliens have been communicating with Australian Aborigines for 70,000 years. What are the Sky Being's relationship with these people?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: What are UFOs? Are they spacecraft? Do they travel vast distances to reach planet Earth? From mysterious planets at the edge of the Solar System, to epic journeys beyond the boundaries of time and space.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Nearly three hundred million people worldwide claim to have been abducted by aliens. Many report being subjected to torturous medical experiments. Others return with unwelcome reminders of their ordeal. Are aliens creating human hybrids?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: In the 1960s we took our first steps into a vast new realm-bound for the Moon. But NASA astronauts would soon find they weren't the only ones out there.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Some experts believe many atmospheric light shows are actually caused by extraterrestrials. Do they pose an imminent threat to humanity? Join us as the alien secrets behind atmospheric anomalies.

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Millions of people believe extraterrestrial live on Earth. Are the aliens here to enlighten us or destroy us? What if the worst-case scenario happened? What would aliens do? And how would they do it?

programme.title: Hauntings
programme.desc: When Andrea Perron moved into her new home in Rhode Island with her parents and four sisters, the previous occupants seemed in a hurry to leave. 'For the sake of your family, leave the lights on in this house at night,' they told her father, Roger. Soon the Perrons were experiencing multiple disturbances, hearing whispers and seeing visions.

programme.title: Ghost Dimension
programme.desc: Could a cemetery be haunted? The team come head out to find out and contact restless souls that have been haunting the graveyard.

programme.title: Ghost Dimension
programme.desc: The team head to Speke Airport to investigate claims that some of the aircraft located there, have ghostly passengers that are still aboard, waiting to take flight.
programme.sub-title: Spirits Flying High at Speke Aerodrome

programme.title: Historic Hauntings
programme.desc: Explore the Palace of Hampton Court, Britain's most haunted site. Learn of the spectral corridor where Catherine Howard, accused of adultery, desperately sought Henry VIII's forgiveness in vain. Discover tales of a midnight-bathing girl at Silent Pool and an ill-fated young woman's restless spirit post-beheading.

programme.title: Paranormal Files: Extraordinary Stories - Ordinary People
programme.desc: For decades, Kent's Blue Bell Hill has been the site of mysterious phenomena. Rumored ghost sightings have haunted the pastoral site. Explore the haunting legacy of Blue Bell Hill in this episode.
programme.sub-title: The Mystery of Blue Bell Hill

programme.title: Paranormal Files: Extraordinary Stories - Ordinary People
programme.desc: This episode explores the paranormal mysteries surrounding an August 2000 Briton sighting, where police crossed paths with a strange light in the sky.

programme.title: The Diary Of Jack The Ripper
programme.desc: Step by painstaking step, the diary is analyzed, verified, and questioned; experts pit their knowledge against the information in the diary; gradually and remorselessly the evidence against Maybrick mounts - until his identity is beyond reasonable doubt. Was Maybrick Jack The Ripper? A complete history of the chilling JTR murders with graphic photos, sickening details and documented evidence.

programme.title: The SS and The Occult
programme.desc: This powerful film revisits the sites most closely associated with Heinrich Himmler and traces the development of his warped ideology. Heinrich Himmler was the creator of the infamous Gestapo, the Waffen SS and the concentration camp network. He was inspired by mystic visions, runes, horoscopes and a longing for a heroic German past. The occult roots of the Third Reich are discussed.

programme.title: The Real Merlin
programme.desc: His name conjures up images of a golden age of magic, mystery and chivalry. Of Camelot and the search for the Holy Grail, King Arthur and his Knights of the Round Table. But is there any truth behind the myth of Merlin, a man beyond the legend? The Real Merlin finds a sixth-century druid, shaman and right-hand man to the last pagan king, a prophet who predicted his own strange three-fold death.

programme.title: World's Greatest Mysteries
programme.desc: Bigfoot. Sasquatch. Yeti. Yeren.Yowie. There are reports the world over of these terrifying creatures. This program shows a chilling eyewitness encounter plus scientific analysis of the creature's footprints providing startling insights into this mystery.
programme.sub-title: Bigfoot: Living Creature or Legendary Lie?

programme.title: The Conspiracy Show with Richard Syrett
programme.desc: In this re-examination of the assassination of civil rights leader Martin Luther King, Richard talks to various researchers who offer evidence that, James Earl Ray, was not the real triggerman. The researchers claim the plot was arranged by the highest levels of government and law enforcement. A noted debunker in the skeptic community refutes these claims as inaccurate.

programme.title: The Conspiracy Show with Richard Syrett
programme.desc: According to a poll conducted by The Roper Organization in 1992, 3.7 million Americans could have been alien abductees. Richard interviews two supposed alien abductees about their claims they were on an alien space craft. He'll also speak with a top abduction researcher who has worked with over a hundred of abductees. However, a skeptic gives a greedier explanation for the abduction phenomenon.

programme.title: EXtraterrestrials: They are Among Us
programme.desc: The encounters in the fourth phase are terrible; the witness not only sees the alleged ship or its crew, but is taken, generally unconscious or against their will, into said ships. Some, like Próspera Muñoz, who gave us in her last interview, possibly the most credible abduction account in our story, return to tell what happened. She is not the only one, as we will see in this exciting chapter.

programme.title: EXtraterrestrials: They are Among Us
programme.desc: In Dec 1995-Mar 1996, a surge of UFO sightings occurred, notably at Polvorin of As Gándaras, Lugo. Military witnessed triangle lights on infrared cameras, marking our longest and most prolific UFO event. Cases included landings and encounters with mysterious lights and alleged crews. A year prior, 'something' crashed from space in Cando de Arriba mountains, A Coruña, igniting the phenomenon.
programme.sub-title: UFOs in Spain - The Last Great Wave

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: For decades, citizen UFOlogists have coordinated alien information-sharing networks, subverting the classified intelligence of their governments. What do these classified documents say about the way that our governments watch the skies?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: The sun. It's an immense powerhouse on a scale that almost defies the imagination. And it's the source of all life here on Earth. But what if that power was being tampered with? Are UFOs really visiting our Sun?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Each year, there are thousands of UFO sightings all over the world. What are these different kind of UFOs? What is each craft's purpose? What powers them and how they are controlled? And most importantly- who is flying them?

programme.title: Unsealed Alien Files
programme.desc: Aborigines have the oldest continuous culture on Earth. Rock paintings and ancient legends suggest that aliens have been communicating with Australian Aborigines for 70,000 years. What are the Sky Being's relationship with these people?

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files examines whether time travel is real and, if it is, whether it is under the control of a mysterious elite. It examines the mysterious South Fork Bridge photo which purports to show a man out of time. It also looks at theories that claim that the Nazis developed a time travel device during World War II.

programme.title: Unsealed Conspiracy Files
programme.desc: Unsealed: Conspiracy Files examines whether the United States government is preparing for a possible alien attack. It looks at a recent report of a joint naval mission by the U.S. and China to combat a hostile alien force over the Pacific Ocean.

programme.title: Homeless For The Holidays
programme.desc: When an uncaring executive falls from the corporate ladder, he learns how difficult it can be to find work and compassion in today's economy. He eventually accepts a humiliating job, but with bills rapidly piling up, and not enough money to go around, he quickly discovers that, unless something changes soon, he'll lose everything by Christmas. Will family and faith be enough to bring joy when you're Homeless for The Holidays?

programme.title: By God's Grace
programme.desc: In the tradition of a classic "A Christmas Carol", this film offers many lessons on the importance of giving and the cause and effect our choices have on others.

programme.title: Hank's Christmas Wish
programme.desc: "Hank's Christmas Wish" tells the heartwarming tale of a retired elf seeking a life of seclusion. However, his plans are interrupted when a group of unrelentingly cheerful townsfolk, brimming with the holiday spirit, come into his life. Through their unwavering kindness and infectious joy, they help him rediscover the true meaning of Christmas. Packed with yuletide laughter, chestnut-roasting moments, and Jack Frost-nipping faith, this cutesy film captures the essence of the holiday season.

programme.title: Christmas Oranges

programme.desc: John Christie kills at least eight women during the 1940s and 1950s, including his wife; he eluded capture for many years.

programme.desc: Dubbed "The Most Evil Conman Ever" by the British press, Hendy-Freegard terrorized victims into believing they were terrorist targets.

programme.title: The Interrogation Room Hosted by Vivica A. Fox
programme.desc: Vivica examines the case of double-murderer Cheyanne Jessie. On August 1, 2015, police received a call from Cheyanne Jessie in which she claimed her father Mark Weekly and daughter Meredith were missing.

programme.title: Crimes Uncovered
programme.desc: The treacherous story of a man who wore many masks and one that finally earned him the title of one of South Africa's worst serial rapists.
programme.sub-title: Lost Innocence: The Fanwell Khumalo Story

programme.title: Becoming Evil: Secret Language of Serial Killers
programme.desc: Discover how killers like Williamn Hearns and Ted Kaczynski use their crime scenes as a form of self-expression, and how profilers and investigators piece together the clues left at these gruesome art exhibits to solve the case.

programme.title: The Real Manhunter

programme.title: The Real Manhunter
programme.desc: Clare Bernal and Michael Pech had only been on three dates when Pech began a campaign of stalking Clare. However, out on bail, and awaiting sentencing, Pech chose a dark path.

programme.title: Nurses Who Kill
programme.desc: Wettlaufer, 49, of Ontario, intentionally administered fatal doses of drugs to her victims, aged 75 to 96, between 2007 and 2014. After killing, she would post some of her dozens of verses on the Allpoetry.com website. Wettlaufer's victims included five women and three men - all of whom were patients at Caressant Care nursing homes in Ontario, where Wettlaufer had worked.

programme.title: Nurses Who Kill
programme.desc: Megan Haines nursed patients at St Andrews Village Nursing Home where she also nursed a lethal grudge. Complaints had been made about the rudeness she'd shown towards patients. Her retaliation? She killed two elderly residents and tried to kill a third. The daughter of one victim, Charli Darragh, gives an emotional interview about the moment she discovered her mother had been murdered.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: Marc Van Beers, a 36-year-old Brussels tax lawyer, dies in a car accident while on his honeymoon; Marc's wife, Aurore, isn't injured in the accident and the case is quickly dismissed; Marc's family is suspicious of Aurore.

programme.title: US Bounty Hunters
programme.desc: Defendant wanted for dealing and possession found hiding in a closet at grandmas.

programme.title: US Bounty Hunters
programme.desc: This guy may have thought the bondsman rescheduled his court date...But he still has to go with the Bounty Hunters.

programme.title: Deadly Standoffs
programme.desc: The Waco siege, a 51-day standoff involving the Branch Davidians in 1993, left nearly 80 people dead.

programme.title: 72 Hours: True Crime
programme.desc: When a senior citizen is killed on a city street, authorities at first treat it as a typical hit-and-run accident.

programme.title: 72 Hours: True Crime
programme.desc: Two murders of mothers in their own homes send shock-waves through a normally quiet and friendly town where everybody leaves their doors unlocked.

programme.title: Inside Crime Scene
programme.desc: In the 1920s, Singapore was likened to notorious Chicago, it topped the crime list in the Straits Settlements and Malaya.

programme.title: Autopsy: The Last Hours of...

programme.title: Crimes Uncovered

programme.sub-title: Sordid Lies: The Cezanne Visser Story

programme.desc: A review of all the cases covered in the series.

programme.title: Murder Maps
programme.desc: On a hot summers day in 1934, a horrifying discovery was made in a trunk at the left luggage office of Brighton Train Station.

programme.title: Mind Investigators
programme.desc: On November 20th 2013, a fishermen discovers the corpse of a baby on the beach of Berck.

programme.title: The Interrogation Room Hosted by Vivica A. Fox
programme.desc: Linda Riley was reported missing when a neighbor couldn't contact her and signs of a struggle were discovered in her home. The race is on to try and find Linda safe and well.

programme.title: Crimes Uncovered
programme.desc: The discovery of two dead bodies dumped in a sugar cane field in a quiet town reveals the possibility of a serial killer.
programme.sub-title: Time of Terror: Sugar Cane Serial Killer Part 1

programme.title: Becoming Evil: Secret Language of Serial Killers
programme.desc: Talk about body language. See how serial killers like the Night Stalker use their victims as just another way to get their message out to the world.

programme.title: Caught on Bodycam
programme.desc: Raw bodycam footage capturing high-stake police incidents.

programme.title: Caught on Bodycam
programme.desc: Raw bodycam footage capturing high-stake police incidents.

programme.title: Nurses Who Kill
programme.desc: Efren Saldivar confessed to killing 40 to 50 patients over an eight-year period. Quickly christened an "Angel of Death," he targeted patients who were already near death. Statistical analysis indicates that the total number of murders committed by Saldivar could be as high as 200, but the bodies were cremated after death long before he owned up to his deeds on the wards.

programme.title: Nurses Who Kill
programme.desc: Megan Haines nursed patients at St Andrews Village Nursing Home where she also nursed a lethal grudge. Complaints had been made about the rudeness she'd shown towards patients. Her retaliation? She killed two elderly residents and tried to kill a third. The daughter of one victim, Charli Darragh, gives an emotional interview about the moment she discovered her mother had been murdered.

programme.title: Under Arrest
programme.desc: Suspect high on drugs is subdued with a taser, police attend a call of shots fired and a stolen vehicle is chased.
programme.sub-title: You're Going to Get a Headache

programme.title: Under Arrest
programme.desc: A jealous lover holds a baseball bat, a nationwide warrant suspect is captured and a carjacker is taken down at gunpoint.

programme.title: Crimes That Made History
programme.desc: 1978 Guyana: Reverend Jim Jones holds an apocalyptic mass. Its outcome was the sacrifice of 918 members of the Peoples Temple - an American cult founded in the middle of the 1950s. The entire world was horrified by the journalists' accounts and the images from Jonestown. This tragedy haunted the hopes of small communities and alternative spiritualities in the 70s.
programme.sub-title: The Jonestown Massacre: An American Apocalypse (1978)

programme.title: Crimes That Made History
programme.desc: On 31 August 1997, Princess Diana died alongside her companion, Dodi Al-Fayed, in a car crash in Paris, whilst being pursued by paparazzi. Her untimely death prompted an outpouring of grief in Britain and elsewhere in the world, and made her a symbol of the excesses of media intrusion, that was ironically echoed in the coverage of her funeral, broadcast live around the globe.

programme.title: Killer Mysteries
programme.desc: A woman is gunned down in the parking lot of her therapist's office building.

programme.title: Killer Mysteries
programme.desc: The search for a local businesswoman who vanished without a trace morphs into a homicide investigation.

programme.title: Deadly Standoffs
programme.desc: Leroy Schweitzer breaks away from the U.S. and takes advantage of everyone who decides to follow him, resulting in a prolonged armed standoff in 1996.

programme.title: French Fridays
programme.desc: Prepare to feast on fantastic French cuisine on Xumo Free Food TV, as top chefs cook up culinary masterpieces right in your living room!

programme.title: Grow Cook Eat
programme.desc: Many people have an aversion to beetroot because the only way they have ever tasted it is boiled and drowned in vinegar! If this is your experience, it deserves a second chance as it is a fine root crop. Beetroot is easy to grow, can be eaten all year round as it stores well, is incredibly good for you, and has multiple uses. You can boil it, bake it, grate it into salads, chutneys, wine, cakes.

programme.title: Grow Cook Eat
programme.desc: Although it's hard to beat the nostalgic crunch of a head of lettuce, most of us have come to expect much more from our salads than crunch. Today, a top notch salad contains many different colours, shapes, sizes, textures and flavours. As well as lettuces, it may also include the leaves of Arugula, Radicchio, Spinach, Cress, Mustards and Herbs.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: In this episode, Lidia prepares three regional Italian dishes- from Piedmont to Tuscany to Emilia Romagna. Her colorful Peppers Piedmontese are a great addition to any antipasto or buffet table, her Malfada Michelangelo Style is a delicious pasta dish based on dish attributed to Michelangelo. lastly, she shares a Filet Mignon Italian Style with Balsamic Reduction using this liquid gold from the area of Modena.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: Lidia fell in love with the Soup and Sandwhich concept shortly after she arrived in America. And soups are one of her favorite creations to make. In this episode, she prepares a velvety Spinach and ChickpeaSoup; an Italian style Baked Toast Sandwhich and to finish, she enjoys some oatmeal crepes with her grandson Ethan.

programme.title: Struggle Meals
programme.desc: Everyone loves carbs! Endlessly versatile, cheap, and super filling - Frankie shows you tricks for pasta, pizza dough, and delicious, easy ramen meals that aren't soup.

programme.title: Blind Tasting Sessions
programme.desc: Spouses Sara and Jonah, of True North Wine Merchants and Frog's Leap Winery, blind taste each other.

programme.title: Blind Tasting Sessions
programme.desc: The Little Nell coworkers throwdown in this blind tasting session at the Food & Wine Classic.

programme.title: John & Lisa's Weekend Kitchen
programme.desc: John and Lisa prepare a gorgeous fish pie, the perfect roast beef and gravy as well as a classic meatloaf with a modern twist.

programme.title: John & Lisa's Weekend Kitchen
programme.desc: Josh and Lisa share some recipes to kick off the new year, including a homemade granola and stewed fruit.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: Cucumbers with whole wheat couscous; toasted grain soup; baked whole wheat penne and ceci beans.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: Clam and scallion risotto with tomatoes; Neapolitan rice and meat mould served with a green salad.

programme.title: Every Bite Takes You Home
programme.desc: Each episode of Every Bite Takes You Home invites you to share in the journeys of remarkable refugees.

programme.title: Feed My Soul, V!
programme.desc: Vanessa takes on take-out with a menu of homemade favorites and a table to match! There's pepperoni naan pizzas, salmon burgers, chicken fingers, a crudite platter, dips, and so much more!

programme.title: Zach Kinda Cooks
programme.desc: Lazy and curmudgeonly chef and ex-Gusto writer Zach cooks one of his all-time favorite dishes - The Rochester Garbage Plate! While cooking, he tells aimless stories, cracks bad jokes, and berates Sydney, the beleaguered camera person.

programme.title: Tastes Like Home
programme.desc: On Tastes Like Home it's a little different this week, as we receive a request from husband and wife Jason & Maire in Kerry - Marie is Swedish but now lives in the Gap of Dunlop and she is about gave birth to twin boys and is keen to learn who to make her dad's Smogsboard with meatballs so she can teach her sons in time.
programme.sub-title: Stockholm, Sweden / Gap of Dunloe, Killarney

programme.title: V is for Vino
programme.desc: Southern Rhône may be the most beautiful wine region in France! Travel with Vince and his buddy Sarkis on a road trip through stunning landscapes, quaint villages, ancient geography, and tons of vineyards, all winding along the Rhône River.

programme.title: Getting Grilled with Curtis Stone
programme.desc: Maks Chmerkovskiy dances his way into Curtis' Kitchen but can Curtis change Maks' mind about Indian Food?

programme.title: Gordon's Great Escape
programme.desc: Gordon ends his travels to India by heading south, living in an ashram in Kerala and working alongside one of India's top chefs in Mumbai.

programme.title: Bring On The Karbs
programme.desc: Chefs Erica and Josh Karbelnik put their heads together to design a three-course menu, highlighting the gifts of the forest! Mushrooms, venison, cranberries, and - of course - black forest cake!

programme.title: Accidental Chef
programme.desc: This week, Melvyn finds himself in South Korea. He experiences two distinctly different cultures and cuisines of the country- that of the royalties and the monks. He meets royal food expert to learn about the imperial traditions and cuisines, which had influenced so much of Korea. Then Melvyn goes zen with a famous Korean monk.

programme.title: Food Pop
programme.desc: The hamburger is one of the most recognizable foods in the world. While the early origins of the burger are often debated, the American hamburger, made from a ground beef patty-sandwiched between two slices of bread-and dressed with classic condiments like lettuce, tomatoes, pickles, and onions, is the most popular version in the world. Even though the hamburger is aniconic part of American cuisine-the burger-is a food that truly belongs to the world.

programme.title: What's Cooking in the World?
programme.desc: Discover the world through some of the most delicious and unusual dishes from countries like China, Morocco and Venezuela. In each episode, we will explore colourful local markets, discovering new flavours and regional produce. The ingredients we find will form the basis for some very special dishes that are simple to make at home.

programme.title: The F Word
programme.desc: In tonight's episode, best British restaurant The Pheasant and best Thai restaurant Simply Thai will be joined by Greek Retsina, to compete for a place in the grand final at the F Word restaurant.

programme.title: Eat Me (Or Try Not To)

programme.title: Destruction Decoded
programme.desc: When water unleashes its rage upon the planet, it becomes the ultimate bringer of death; whether it's from rain washing over the ground, rivers bursting their banks, or failed efforts to stem the flow, flooding is as inevitable as it is unstoppable.

programme.title: Destruction Decoded
programme.desc: Bridges and tunnels revolutionized transportation-but when they fail, tragedy follows. This episode explores the world's worst collapses and fires, including a tunnel blaze in the Alps so intense it fused 20 cars together. As we build bigger and faster, we also raise the stakes.

programme.title: Jeremy Pang's Asian Kitchen

programme.title: Mexico: One Plate at a Time with Rick Bayless
programme.desc: The Caribbean Sea provides bountiful fish, aptly translated on the plate through ceviche. Meet Chefs Pedro Abascal, Xavier Perez Stone, and Diego Lopez who reveal their own delectable ceviches, and visit Rick's new restaurant, Lena Brava.

programme.title: Mexico: One Plate at a Time with Rick Bayless
programme.desc: So many moles, so little time. Rick will focus on two moles while visiting the Seasons of My Heart Cooking School on the outskirts of Oaxaca City to explore Black Mole and Green Mole with school owner Susana Trilling and her students.
programme.sub-title: Oaxaca, the Land of Seven Moles

programme.title: Andiamo! Uptown
programme.desc: Back to the snow Donna goes, but this time, you and she will explore Quebec City, North America's oldest city, and experience its local culture, cuisine, and its most renowned hotel. Plus, visit the famous Ice Hotel.

programme.title: The Toque 12
programme.desc: Professional Mixologist Jonas Ax reveals his depth of knowledge of all things shaken, stirred, chilled, and sparkling as host Phillip Davenport spends an afternoon at Elysium Bar and Terrace.

programme.title: The Toque 12
programme.desc: Nestled in the St. Regis Resort in Bali, the Pan-Asian inspired haute cuisine found at Kayuputi Restaurant perfectly captures the dreamlike setting of the St. Regis Resort. Join Phil as he explores Kayuputi's heavenly signature dishes.

programme.title: Ottolenghi's Mediterranean Feast
programme.desc: Yotam explores Israel's fresh produce and seafood, and cooks with cutting edge chefs. Excited by the country's abundance of fruit and vegetables, he also travels to a remote farm, and forages for ingredients in the hills of Jerusalem.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge's Proper Pub Food
programme.desc: Tom prepares decadent, showstopping dishes for special occasions, including an elegant asparagus served with his ultimate salad dressing, a slow-roast duck, deep-fried oysters, spiced monkfish, and a refreshing gin and tonic granita.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Smoke
programme.desc: Steven Raichlen prepares Cold Smoked Scallops with Smoked Tomatoes, Jicama-Mango Salsa, Slow-Roasted Chicken with Horseradish Dip and Smoked Baby Back Ribs with Prickly Pear Barbecue Sauce.

programme.title: What's Eating Harlem
programme.desc: The Harlem Chocolate Factory is a little slice of chocolate heaven, SoHarlem Inc. and Young Atlas are helping create sustainable economic development in Harlem, and Ortomare Ristorante Pizzeria brings the taste and appeal of Rome to N.Y.C.

programme.title: The Toque 12 - Master Chefs
programme.desc: Executive Chef Sabrina Stillhart shares the secrets behind a few of Gordon Ramsay's enticing signature dishes at Bread Street Kitchen, Gordon chooses an intern for his restaurant in Singapore, and taste some whisky with "Mr. Whisky."

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Smoke
programme.desc: Everyone loves a cocktail party, especially when you infuse the menu with the intoxicating aroma of wood smoke. Check out these smokehouse recipes inspired by diverse cuisines from Spain to Australia.

programme.title: The Toque 12
programme.desc: Alila Villas Uluwatu is a magical 5-star resort set atop steep cliffs overlooking the Indian Ocean. Executive Chef Stephane Simond prepares stunning dishes served at Alila's two high end restaurants CIRE and The Warung.

programme.title: Mexico: One Plate at a Time with Rick Bayless
programme.desc: Rick and local guide Luis Garduno of REDTours venture out on a skiff to learn about sustainable fishing on Magdalena Bay. They catch up with local lobster fishermen and clam divers and follow that up with shore lunch on Isla de Magdalena.
programme.sub-title: A Delicious Feast in Magdalena Bay

programme.title: Ottolenghi's Mediterranean Island Feast
programme.desc: On the stunning island of Corsica, Yotam discovers how the local terrain, called the maquis, is infused in the flavors of the food when he meets with the island's most celebrated chefs and food producers who share the cuisine they love.

programme.title: Primal Grill with Steven Raichlen
programme.desc: Americans eat less than 1 pound of lamb per year, but globally, pit masters grill more lamb than any other meat. From Morocco to New Zealand, lamb reigns. You can't be a well-rounded grill master until you've perfected grilling lamb.

programme.title: Jeremy Pang's Asian Kitchen
programme.desc: At the barbecue, Jeremy cooks up Korean BBQ Beef and Banchan, and for dessert, a Macha Mille Crepe Cake.

programme.title: Dream of Italy
programme.desc: In Chianti, we celebrate true Chianti at Castello di Ama, and at Busatti in Anghiari, 100-year-old looms craft fine fabrics. We will also hunt wild boar and meet butcher Dario Cecchini in Panzano, and ride with the butteri in Maremma.

programme.title: My Greek Table with Diane Kochilas
programme.desc: Naxos is famed for the quality of its meats, its seductive array of cheeses, and its potatoes. From the Mediterranean shore Diane and Alexis travel to a remote mountain hideaway where a pair of local cooks await with a classic Naxos feast.
programme.sub-title: Naxos: Meat and Potatoes Like You've Never Had 'em

programme.title: Taste Hunters
programme.desc: At the foot of the Pyrenees Mountains in southwestern France, the Basque country is home to a diverse agricultural heritage formed by countless family farms where traditional farming methods continue to be practiced and preserved.

programme.title: Tastes Like Home
programme.desc: What dish would most remind Sarah-Jo of her family in Gorey? Her mother Marian's Chicken Paprika dish. Catherine travels to Boston where she will prepare Sarah-Jo's favorite dish for her, while also exploring Boston's exciting city life.

programme.title: Traveling with Denella Ri'chard
programme.desc: Denella is in St. Croix, the US Virgin Islands. From sunrise to sunset, there is so much to do in and out of the blue sapphire waters. She indulges in the island's cuisine and drinks with some very peculiar locals.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Fire
programme.desc: Steven serves rum and citrus-glazed jumbo shrimp grilled on sugarcane, "finger-burner" lamb chops from Spain, and Smoked Nectarine Bellinis. Sommelier Kristine Bocchino shares wine suggestions to keep the party flowing.

programme.title: Jeremy Pang's Asian Kitchen
programme.desc: Jeremy then makes Tea Smoked Duck and Pancakes, followed by a Macanese Egg Tart, the perfect accompaniment for a cup of tea. Jeremy's iconic first dish is Crispy Belly Pork.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Smoke
programme.desc: Don't wait for Thanksgiving to try these twists on holiday favorites: whiskey-brined turkey smoked over maple wood, bacon-stuffed onions, smoky creamed corn, fiery jalapeno cranberry salsa, and smoky bacon-apple crisp.

programme.title: Travels with Darley
programme.desc: Immerse yourself in a melting pot of cultures in Prince William County, Virginia. Learn about the history of the Civil War and visit a CIA training ground. Experience one-of-a-kind travel gems and truly memorable cuisine with Darley.

programme.title: Culinary Travels With Dave Eckert
programme.desc: In the second part of our exciting trip to Mendoza, Argentina we will taste and experience some of the most notable wines in the world.

programme.title: My Greek Table with Diane Kochilas
programme.desc: In this love song to her adopted city, Diane explores the hip side of Athens that tourists seldom get to see. Nowhere is the Athens vibe more evident than in the modern, yet deeply rooted, cuisine that defines Athens' modern food culture.

programme.title: Primal Grill with Steven Raichlen
programme.desc: In this show, we dive into the art of spit-roasting. Learn how to grill a sausage and cheese-stuffed rib roast, roast a Greek-style whole hog over wood, and cook Moroccan-style lamb ribs perfectly on a gas-fired rotisserie.

programme.title: Primal Grill with Steven Raichlen
